text:
Registered residential sales reached 11,608 units valued at AED 34,328,091,812 over the last four weeks, marking an 11.4 percent increase in volume and a 25.6 percent rise in value compared to the previous four-week period. Mortgage registrations totaled 4,630, which are tracked separately from sales transactions. The off-plan share of sales stood at 57.2 percent, down from 65.4 percent in the prior period.

The median residential price per square foot rose to AED 1,688, a 0.8 percent increase from AED 1,675 in the previous four weeks. Top sales areas by 12-week volume include Dubai South with 3,732 sales and Jumeirah Village Circle with 2,302 sales. Business Bay recorded a 6.1 percent decline in median price per square foot over 12 weeks, while Majan saw a 1.8 percent increase.

Rental activity showed 91,550 Ejari contracts registered, with 51.3 percent classified as renewals. The median residential rent was AED 69,769 per year. Estimated gross yields for flats were highest in Zaabeel First at 9.0 percent and International City Phase 1 at 8.6 percent. Town Square, Dubai Sports City, and Dubai Production City followed with yields of 6.9 percent, 6.7 percent, and 6.5 percent respectively.

The watch list highlights Al Yufrah 1 with a 43.3 percent 12-week price increase and Dubai Industrial City up 12.9 percent. Conversely, Palm Jumeirah cooled by 16.6 percent and Palm Deira by 13.4 percent. Anomaly monitoring identified 1,002 residential sales in the last 60 days priced more than 35 percent away from their comparable cell median. Figures are based on registered DLD data and Ejari contracts using medians and benchmark filters that exclude bulk deals, partial shares, and statistical outliers.

facts.ranking_rule: communities with at least 30 eligible sales in both 12-week windows; yields also need 30 rent contracts of the same property type
